prompt: Render a polished, buildable native Windows 11 desktop app screen for Freehand, a tray-first local dictation utility. Landscape 3:2 composition, crisp readable UI text, app filling the frame, Windows minimize/maximize/close controls at top right. This is an actual working product concept, not a marketing page or design presentation. Use familiar native buttons, inputs, navigation and icons. Dark appearance. Real navigation labels: History, Dictionary, Settings. Search history scopes only the history. Synthetic sample transcripts, shared across concepts: Today 10:42: "Keep the input device selected while recording. If the microphone disconnects, preserve the recording and offer Retry." Today 10:18: "The settings change should take effect after the current recording finishes." Yesterday 16:05: "Review the dictionary corrections before the next release." Actions are Copy and Delete. No usage metrics or invented features. A small floating status pill at the bottom center shows a red recording dot, a restrained white waveform, "Recording", and "00:12". It is secondary to the window content. No tagline or explanatory helper copy. Lead with a compact single-column transcript-first layout. A slim top bar carries Freehand at left and History, Dictionary, Settings as clear text tabs, with History selected. No sidebar. Below a quiet History heading and search field, show three dated transcripts as readable text blocks separated by space and the lightest rules. The newest is fully readable with Copy and a discreet overflow action. Avoid large cards and nested boxes. The world is modern information wayfinding translated into a quiet utility: flat graphite ground, soft near-white type, a very restrained muted sage selection treatment only where useful. Native sans with sentence-case controls, clear hierarchy, deliberate open space. Its signature is that the selected transcript owns its small inline action area, leaving other entries to read like text. No decorative background, vintage elements, big record button, or marketing language.
approval: Sam selected Compact and requested its clickable prototype on October 22, 2026.
